title: Directional observation kernels can hide distinct positive distributions
problem: Distinguish a rectangular Pascal probability law from nonnegative rivals using complete directional marginals.
failure: R05's lesson warns against assuming multiple observations determine the full distribution; axis and both diagonal projections still admit distinct positive distributions on a 4 by 4 grid.
correction: Represent directional projection kernels using primitive binomial factors and their product. Compare its bidegree to the supported rectangle, and verify the resulting nullity with exact matrix rank. Construct a positive rival and test mixed moments and convolution.
transfer: Measure the actual joint observation kernel before choosing additional sensors. Distinguish exact algebraic identifiability from stability under noise; a new direction can remove ambiguity even if repeated observations in old directions do not.
limits: Switching-component theorem and dimension are established prior art (Hajdu and Tijdeman, 2001). R06 is a session-derived Pascal application with bounded local exact tests; no originality or independent validation claim, no physical or noisy-data inference. Full axis marginals constrain nonnegative competitors to the rectangle.
author: TOTO; established switching-component theory credited to Hajdu and Tijdeman in source
